title: Module 1: Claude Platform & Solution Design
description: Reference architecture, model selection, context strategy, and design principles for Claude-based solutions.

questions.question: In the Claude Platform reference architecture, which layer is responsible for translating business requirements into technical designs?
options: Integration Layer
Application/Orchestration Layer
Foundation Model Layer
Business Strategy Layer
questions.explanation: The Application/Orchestration Layer sits between the foundation model and business logic, translating requirements into Claude-powered technical designs.

questions.question: When selecting between Claude models for a production solution, which factor should an architect prioritize for a real-time customer-facing chatbot with strict latency requirements?
options: Maximum context window size
Latency and throughput characteristics
Number of available API endpoints
Support for the widest range of tools
questions.explanation: For real-time customer-facing applications, latency and throughput are the primary selection criteria, as they directly impact user experience.

questions.question: What is the recommended approach for managing context window usage in a long-running Claude-based agentic workflow?
options: Use the largest available context window regardless of cost
Implement a sliding window with selective context retention and summarization of older turns
Reset the conversation after every tool call
Store all conversation history in an external database and never pass it to the model
questions.explanation: A sliding window with selective retention balances context awareness with cost and performance, keeping recent turns and summaries of earlier ones.

questions.question: Which Claude Platform capability enables you to combine multiple specialized models or endpoints within a single solution?
options: Model routing and multi-model orchestration
Single-model fine-tuning
API rate limiting
Context window expansion
questions.explanation: Model routing allows architects to direct different tasks to the most appropriate Claude model variant or endpoint based on complexity, latency, or cost requirements.

questions.question: In a Claude-based solution architecture, what is the primary purpose of the 'guardrails' layer?
options: Improve response speed
Filter and validate inputs/outputs to ensure safety, compliance, and quality
Manage user authentication
Optimize token usage
questions.explanation: Guardrails provide input/output filtering to enforce safety policies, prevent data leakage, and ensure outputs meet quality and compliance standards.

questions.question: When designing a multi-agent Claude solution, what is the key architectural pattern recommended by Anthropic?
options: A hub-and-spoke pattern where a central orchestrator delegates to specialized agent tools
Each agent operates completely independently with no coordination
All agents share a single prompt and context window
Agents communicate exclusively through a shared database
questions.explanation: The hub-and-spoke pattern uses Claude as a central orchestrator that delegates tasks to specialized tool-calling agents, maintaining control and context management.

questions.question: Which design principle should guide the separation of concerns in a Claude-based enterprise solution?
options: Put all logic into a single monolithic prompt
Separate prompt engineering, tool definitions, and business logic into distinct, independently testable layers
Embed all tool definitions inside the system prompt
Avoid modularization to reduce latency
questions.explanation: Separating concerns allows independent testing, iteration, and governance of prompts, tools, and business logic.

questions.question: For a document-processing pipeline using Claude, what is the most cost-effective strategy for handling large documents?
options: Send the entire document in a single API call
Chunk the document strategically, process chunks with appropriate models, and use a final synthesis step
Always use the smallest model regardless of task complexity
Avoid document processing and only handle structured data
questions.explanation: Strategic chunking with model selection per chunk (e.g., smaller models for extraction, larger for synthesis) optimizes both cost and quality.

questions.question: What role does 'prompt caching' play in Claude solution design?
options: It eliminates the need for any prompt engineering
It reduces latency and cost by reusing previously processed prompt prefixes across requests
It automatically generates prompts from business requirements
It increases the context window size
questions.explanation: Prompt caching stores frequently-used prompt prefixes, reducing both latency and cost when those prefixes are reused across multiple requests.

questions.question: In Claude's architecture, what is the relationship between the 'system prompt' and 'user messages'?
options: They are identical and interchangeable
The system prompt sets behavior/context for the entire conversation; user messages provide the specific task or input
User messages override the system prompt entirely
The system prompt is only used in the first message and then ignored
questions.explanation: The system prompt establishes persistent behavior and context, while user messages carry the actual task-specific inputs within that framework.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key consideration when designing Claude solutions for multi-tenant enterprise environments?
options: All tenants should share the same API key for simplicity
Tenant data must be isolated; prompts and tools should include tenant-specific context without cross-tenant leakage
Multi-tenancy is not supported by Claude
Each tenant requires a separate Claude model instance
questions.explanation: Proper tenant isolation prevents data leakage while still allowing shared infrastructure, using tenant-specific context injection rather than shared credentials.

questions.question: What is the recommended approach for handling tool call failures in a Claude-based agentic loop?
options: Abort the entire conversation and restart
Implement retry logic with exponential backoff, fallback strategies, and user-facing error messages
Ignore the error and proceed to the next step
Silently retry without informing the user
questions.explanation: Robust error handling includes retries with backoff, alternative paths when possible, and transparent communication with users about failures.

questions.question: When designing a Claude solution that requires real-time data access, which integration pattern is most appropriate?
options: Bake all data into the prompt before each call
Use tool calling to fetch fresh data on-demand during the conversation
Store all real-time data in the system prompt
Avoid real-time data entirely
questions.explanation: Tool calling enables dynamic, real-time data retrieval during a conversation, keeping the context lean while providing up-to-date information when needed.

questions.question: What is the primary benefit of using structured output (JSON mode) in Claude for enterprise applications?
options: It makes responses faster
It guarantees parseable, consistent output that integrates reliably with downstream systems and databases
It reduces the cost of API calls
It eliminates the need for validation
questions.explanation: Structured output ensures predictable, machine-readable responses essential for automated pipelines, database integration, and API consumption.

questions.question: In a Claude-based solution, what is the purpose of a 'retrieval-augmented generation' (RAG) pipeline?
options: To reduce the number of API calls needed
To ground Claude's responses in up-to-date, domain-specific data retrieved from external knowledge bases
To train a custom model
To replace the need for a system prompt
questions.explanation: RAG enriches Claude's responses by retrieving relevant, current information from external sources, grounding answers in specific domain knowledge rather than training data alone.
